audits.title: Can audit improve antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice?
audits.standard: Antibiotic prescribing guidelines issued as part of the audit
audits.setting: 175 general dental practitioners, North West of England

cycle1.result: 2316 antibiotic prescriptions issued; 81% for therapeutic reasons; amoxycillin most commonly prescribed (57.6% overall).

audits.intervention: Audit with an educational component and issuing of guidelines.

cycle2.result: Prescriptions reduced by 42.5% to 1330; antibiotic regimens significantly changed.

audits.other_findings: Sample sizes are numbers of prescriptions from 175 practitioners; other common drugs were metronidazole (23.8%), penicillin (9.3%) and erythromycin (4.8%).
audits.citation: Palmer NA, Dailey YM, Martin MV. Can audit improve antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice?. Br Dent J. 2001;191(5):253-255. doi:10.1038/sj.bdj.4801156a. PMID: 11575760.

audits.title: An audit of antibiotic prescribing by vocational dental practitioners.
audits.standard: Available antibiotic prescribing guidelines for dental practice
audits.setting: Seven vocational training schemes, general dental practice

cycle1.result: Wide variation in therapeutic regimens, most not conforming to guidelines; most VDPs understood prophylaxis for cardiac defects but some prescribed without medical indication.

audits.other_findings: 64 VDPs took part; authors recommend formal antibiotic education in the VT year.
audits.citation: Palmer NO, Batchelor PA. An audit of antibiotic prescribing by vocational dental practitioners. Prim Dent Care. 2004;11(3):77-80. doi:10.1308/1355761041208476. PMID: 15242563.

audits.title: The impact of clinical audit on antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice.
audits.standard: Contemporary antibiotic prescribing guidelines and agreed standards

cycle1.result: 43% of prescriptions error-free in dose, frequency or duration; 29.2% justified.

audits.intervention: Education on prescribing guidelines, presentation of previous errors and agreed standards
audits.other_findings: 212 practitioners took part; amoxicillin and metronidazole were most prescribed.
audits.citation: Chate RA, White S, Hale LR, Howat AP, Bottomley J, Barnet-Lamb J, et al.. The impact of clinical audit on antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice. Br Dent J. 2006;201(10):635-641. doi:10.1038/sj.bdj.4814261. PMID: 17128233.

audits.title: An audit of antimicrobial prescribing in an acute dental care department.
audits.standard: FGDP(UK) and Scottish Dental Clinical Effectiveness guidelines on antimicrobial prescribing; target 100% compliance
audits.setting: Oral surgery acute dental department, Guy's Hospital, London

cycle1.result: 30% of prescriptions appropriate; 62% of practitioners recorded a diagnosis.

audits.intervention: Two-month intervention of extensive training and education of staff and students.

cycle2.result: 80% of prescriptions appropriate; 100% recorded a diagnosis.

audits.other_findings: Most inappropriate prescriptions in both cycles were for acute pulpitis without systemic involvement.
audits.citation: Chopra R, Merali R, Paolinelis G, Kwok J. An audit of antimicrobial prescribing in an acute dental care department. Prim Dent J. 2014;3(4):24-29. doi:10.1308/205016814813877270. PMID: 25668371.

audits.title: A multicentre, multicycle audit of the prescribing practices of three paediatric dental departments in the North of England.
audits.setting: Three paediatric dental departments in the North of England (Sheffield, Liverpool, Manchester)
audits.intervention: Education and provision of an aide-memoire.

cycle2.result: 71% of prescriptions appropriate in the third cycle.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles in total; deficiencies found in all three centres.
audits.citation: Yesudian GT, Gilchrist F, Bebb K, Albadri S, Aspinall A, Swales K, et al.. A multicentre, multicycle audit of the prescribing practices of three paediatric dental departments in the North of England. Br Dent J. 2015;218(12):681-685. doi:10.1038/sj.bdj.2015.440. PMID: 26114702.
